Optional fields:

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime
import numpy as np

# Read the CSV file
df = pd.read_csv('/app/data/Order Details (1).csv')

# Convert date columns to datetime
date_columns = ['Order_Date', 'Processed_Date', 'Shipped_Date', 'Delivery_Date']
for col in date_columns:
    df[col] = pd.to_datetime(df[col], format='%m/%d/%Y')

# Calculate same-month deliveries
same_month_deliveries = (df['Order_Date'].dt.month == df['Delivery_Date'].dt.month) & \
                       (df['Order_Date'].dt.year == df['Delivery_Date'].dt.year)
same_month_percentage = round((same_month_deliveries.sum() / len(df)) * 100)

# Calculate milestone durations in days
df['ordered_to_processed'] = (df['Processed_Date'] - df['Order_Date']).dt.days
df['processed_to_shipped'] = (df['Shipped_Date'] - df['Processed_Date']).dt.days
df['shipped_to_delivered'] = (df['Delivery_Date'] - df['Shipped_Date']).dt.days

# Calculate average days for each milestone
avg_ordered_to_processed = round(df['ordered_to_processed'].mean(), 1)
avg_processed_to_shipped = round(df['processed_to_shipped'].mean(), 1)
avg_shipped_to_delivered = round(df['shipped_to_delivered'].mean(), 1)

# Industry benchmarks
benchmarks = {
    'ordered_to_processed': 2.0,
    'processed_to_shipped': 2.5,
    'shipped_to_delivered': 4.0
}

# Compare against benchmarks and identify underperforming stages
performance = {
    'ordered_to_processed': avg_ordered_to_processed,
    'processed_to_shipped': avg_processed_to_shipped,
    'shipped_to_delivered': avg_shipped_to_delivered
}

underperforming_stages = []
for stage, avg_time in performance.items():
    if avg_time > benchmarks[stage]:
        underperforming_stages.append(stage)

# Calculate percentage exceeding benchmarks for underperforming stages
exceeding_percentages = {}
for stage in underperforming_stages:
    exceeding_count = (df[stage] > benchmarks[stage]).sum()
    exceeding_percentage = round((exceeding_count / len(df)) * 100)
    exceeding_percentages[stage] = exceeding_percentage

# Generate recommendations
recommendations = {
    'ordered_to_processed': [
        "Implement automated order processing systems to reduce manual handling time",
        "Streamline inventory verification processes",
        "Establish dedicated order processing teams during peak hours",
        "Use real-time inventory management to avoid processing delays"
    ],
    'processed_to_shipped': [
        "Optimize warehouse layout for faster picking and packing",
        "Implement batch processing for similar orders",
        "Establish partnerships with multiple shipping carriers for faster pickup",
        "Invest in automated packaging systems",
        "Improve coordination between processing and shipping teams"
    ],
    'shipped_to_delivered': [
        "Partner with faster shipping carriers or upgrade shipping tiers",
        "Implement regional distribution centers to reduce shipping distances",
        "Offer expedited shipping options",
        "Negotiate better service level agreements with current carriers",
        "Consider last-mile delivery partnerships in major metropolitan areas"
    ]
}

# Write results to output file
with open('/app/output/answer.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write("APPAREL E-COMMERCE ORDER ANALYSIS REPORT\n")
    f.write("=" * 45 + "\n\n")
    
    # Same-month delivery percentage
    f.write(f"1. SAME-MONTH DELIVERY PERFORMANCE\n")
    f.write(f"Percentage of orders delivered in the same month as order placement: {same_month_percentage}%\n\n")
    
    # Average milestone durations
    f.write("2. AVERAGE MILESTONE DURATIONS\n")
    f.write(f"- Ordered to Processed: {avg_ordered_to_processed} days\n")
    f.write(f"- Processed to Shipped: {avg_processed_to_shipped} days\n")
    f.write(f"- Shipped to Delivered: {avg_shipped_to_delivered} days\n\n")
    
    # Benchmark comparison
    f.write("3. INDUSTRY BENCHMARK COMPARISON\n")
    f.write("Stage\t\t\tActual\tBenchmark\tStatus\n")
    f.write("-" * 50 + "\n")
    
    stage_names = {
        'ordered_to_processed': 'Ordered to Processed',
        'processed_to_shipped': 'Processed to Shipped', 
        'shipped_to_delivered': 'Shipped to Delivered'
    }
    
    for stage, avg_time in performance.items():
        benchmark = benchmarks[stage]
        status = "NEEDS IMPROVEMENT" if avg_time > benchmark else "MEETS BENCHMARK"
        f.write(f"{stage_names[stage]}\t{avg_time}\t{benchmark}\t\t{status}\n")
    
    f.write("\n")
    
    # Underperforming stages analysis
    if underperforming_stages:
        f.write("4. UNDERPERFORMING STAGES ANALYSIS\n")
        for stage in underperforming_stages:
            f.write(f"\n{stage_names[stage]}:\n")
            f.write(f"- Average time: {performance[stage]} days (vs benchmark: {benchmarks[stage]} days)\n")
            f.write(f"- Percentage of orders exceeding benchmark: {exceeding_percentages[stage]}%\n")
    
        f.write("\n5. RECOMMENDATIONS FOR IMPROVEMENT\n")
        for stage in underperforming_stages:
            f.write(f"\n{stage_names[stage]} Improvements:\n")
            for i, rec in enumerate(recommendations[stage], 1):
                f.write(f"{i}. {rec}\n")
    else:
        f.write("4. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY\n")
        f.write("All stages meet or exceed industry benchmarks. No immediate improvements needed.\n")

print("Analysis complete. Results written to /app/output/answer.txt")
EOF
